Section 1.  Permitted Transfers.

Tenant may, without Landlord’s consent, assign this Lease or sublet all or any portion of the Leased Premises to: (a) an Affiliate of Tenant; (b) a successor entity resulting from a merger, reorganization, consolidation, or change of control of Tenant, or a purchaser of all or substantially all of Tenant’s assets or equity interests; or (c) any other entity licensed to provide outpatient medical services, provided that, in each case, (i) the assignee or subtenant assumes in writing all of Tenant’s obligations under this Lease, and (ii) Tenant provides Landlord with written notice within thirty (30) days thereafter. As used herein, “Affiliate” means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Tenant.

Tenant may assign this Lease without Landlord’s consent to a true Affiliate under common control or to a successor by merger or sale of substantially all assets, but only if: (a) the transferee’s tangible net worth immediately after the transfer equals or exceeds Tenant’s tangible net worth both on the Commencement Date and immediately before the transfer; (b) the transferee assumes all obligations in writing; (c) the Permitted Use does not change; (d) Tenant delivers notice, financial statements, organizational documents, and licensure evidence at least twenty (20) business days before the transfer, except that notice may follow within ten (10) business days for an internal reorganization that does not change ultimate control; and (e) Tenant and each guarantor remain fully liable. Any merger, reorganization, equity sale, sale of substantially all assets, management agreement, license, concession, or other direct or indirect change of control is a “Transfer.”

Section 2.  Subsequent Clinical Alterations.  Following the Initial Build-Out,

Tenant may, without Landlord’s consent but upon written notice to Landlord, install, modify, remove, and reconfigure examination rooms, treatment areas, privacy partitions, medical equipment, and related non-structural clinical improvements as Tenant’s outpatient service offerings evolve, provided such work does not affect the structural components of the building or reduce the base building electrical capacity available to other tenants. Any alteration affecting structural components, the building envelope, or systems shared with other tenants shall require Landlord’s consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and shall be deemed granted if Landlord fails to respond within ten (10) business days after receipt of Tenant’s complete plans and specifications.

Tenant may perform cosmetic, non-structural alterations costing less than Fifty Thousand Dollars ($50,000) in the aggregate in any twelve (12)-month period without Landlord’s consent upon at least fifteen (15) business days’ prior written notice, provided the work does not affect any base building system, building capacity, the building envelope, or any other tenant. All other alterations require Landlord’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed if the foregoing conditions are satisfied. Tenant shall deliver complete plans before commencing work and as-built drawings within thirty (30) days after completion. No deemed consent shall apply to structural, capacity-affecting, or base building systems work.

Landlord’s Default; Tenant’s Self-Help.
Landlord’s Default.
If Landlord fails to perform

any obligation required of it under this Lease within fifteen (15) days after written notice from Tenant specifying the default (or, for defaults that cannot reasonably be cured within fifteen (15) days, if Landlord fails to commence cure within such period and thereafter diligently prosecute the same to completion), Tenant may, without waiving any other remedy, cure such default on Landlord’s behalf and deduct the reasonable, documented cost thereof, together with interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, from the next installment(s) of Base Rent due under this Lease, in addition to Tenant’s emergency self-help rights under Section 4 of Article VIII.

Section 3.

Tenant’s Election for Significant Damage.  If damage or destruction to the Leased Premises or the building would require more than ninety (90) days to restore, or if the cost to restore the Leased Premises would exceed ten percent (10%) of the replacement cost of the Leased Premises, Tenant may, in its sole discretion, elect to terminate this Lease by written notice to Landlord given within thirty (30) days after the date of such damage or destruction, in which event any unearned rent paid in advance by Tenant shall be refunded and the Security Deposit shall be returned in full.

Termination for Significant Damage.  Either party may terminate this Lease upon thirty (30) days’ written notice if Landlord reasonably estimates that restoration will require more than one hundred eighty (180) days after the later of receipt of insurance proceeds and required permits. Landlord may also terminate if the casualty is uninsured or underinsured, occurs during the last eighteen (18) months of the Term, affects more than fifty percent (50%) of the building’s replacement cost, or if Landlord’s lender requires insurance proceeds to be applied to the debt. Unearned rent and the unapplied Security Deposit shall be returned after Tenant satisfies its surrender obligations.
Section 4.  Landlord’s Failure to Maintain.

If Landlord fails to commence necessary repairs to a building system described in Section 1 of this Article VIII within five (5) business days after written notice from Tenant (or immediately in the case of an emergency affecting patient safety or Tenant’s ability to operate), and such failure materially interferes with Tenant’s ability to safely treat patients, Tenant may, without waiving any other remedy, perform such repairs itself and deduct the reasonable, documented cost thereof, together with interest at the rate set forth in Article XV, from the next installment(s) of Base Rent due under this Lease.

If Landlord fails to commence a repair required under Section 1 within fifteen (15) business days after written notice from Tenant, or such longer period as is reasonably required so long as Landlord promptly commences and diligently pursues the repair, Tenant may pursue its remedies at law or in equity. In an emergency posing an imminent threat to patient safety or rendering the Leased Premises unusable, Tenant may perform only the work reasonably necessary within the Leased Premises after telephonic and written notice and Landlord’s failure to respond, using contractors approved by Landlord where practicable. Landlord shall reimburse reasonable, documented costs properly incurred under the preceding sentence within thirty (30) days after receipt or dispute them in writing. Tenant shall have no right to deduct or offset any amount against Base Rent or Additional Rent.
